# Grokking System Design

> A free, open, pattern-based guide to system design interviews: 30 reusable patterns, 59 question walkthroughs, 19 distributed systems deep dives, 27 cheat sheets, 122 company guides, and 4 study roadmaps. The open companion to the original Grokking the System Design Interview course by DesignGurus.io.

The approach is pattern-based rather than question-based. Instead of memorizing answers to a fixed list of questions, you learn a small set of building blocks (caching, sharding, replication, consistency, messaging) that recur across very different systems, then apply them to whatever question you are asked.

Every page below is plain Markdown and free to read, with no account required. Each description is that page's own one-line summary.

## Start here

- [The system design interview framework](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/interview-framework.md): The seven steps of a 45 minute round, and how many minutes each one deserves.
- [System design in one page](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/system-design-in-one-page.md): The whole framework, the patterns, and the numbers, condensed onto one screen.
- [Glossary](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/glossary.md): Every term used in this repo, defined in one line each.

## Cheat sheets

Quick reference and decision pages. The comparison sheets each start from one question and give the answer you can say out loud.

- [AWS vs GCP vs Azure: the service translation table](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/aws-vs-gcp-vs-azure.md): The same building block under three different names, so you can answer in whatever cloud the interviewer uses.
- [Caching strategies](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/caching-strategies.md): Five ways to keep a cache and a database consistent, and the one question that picks between them.
- [Common mistakes and anti-patterns](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/common-mistakes.md): The errors that cost strong candidates the offer, and what to do instead of each one.
- [Interview communication tips](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/communication-tips.md): How to sound like a senior engineer while you are still working the problem out.
- [Core components reference](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/core-components.md): The building blocks you assemble in almost every design. What each one is, and when to reach for it.
- [DynamoDB vs MongoDB](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/dynamodb-vs-mongodb.md): One question settles this: can you list every query before you design the schema?
- [Back-of-the-envelope estimation](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/estimation.md): The handful of numbers worth memorizing, and how to turn them into a size for any system.
- [System design flashcards](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/flashcards.md): Question and answer cards over every core pattern, for finding the gaps in your recall.
- [The system design interview framework](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/interview-framework.md): The seven steps of a 45 minute round, and how many minutes each one deserves.
- [Kafka vs Kinesis vs Pub/Sub](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/kafka-vs-kinesis-vs-pubsub.md): Three managed streams compared by whose log it is, how capacity is billed, and whether you can replay.
- [Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs SQS](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/kafka-vs-rabbitmq-vs-sqs.md): A log, a broker, or a managed queue: choose by what the consumer needs, not by brand.
- [L4 vs L7 load balancing](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/l4-vs-l7-load-balancing.md): Does the balancer need to read the request to decide where it goes? That one question settles it.
- [Latency numbers: the one-page visual](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/latency-numbers.md): Every latency worth knowing on one ladder, and the design rules that follow from it.
- [A mock interview, annotated: two candidates, one question](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/mock-interview-walkthrough.md): One question answered twice, once as a no-hire and once as a hire, with notes on where each one earned or lost signal.
- [Non-functional requirements](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/non-functional-requirements.md): What a system must *be*, not just what it must *do*. These are the qualities interviewers probe, and the constraints that shape every design decision.
- [PostgreSQL vs DynamoDB vs Cassandra](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/postgres-vs-dynamodb-vs-cassandra.md): The SQL versus NoSQL argument made concrete, with three real stores and the access patterns each one fits.
- [Push vs pull feeds](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/push-vs-pull-feeds.md): Pay for fan-out when the post is written, or when the feed is opened. Accounts with millions of followers decide it.
- [Rate limiting algorithms](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/rate-limiting-algorithms.md): Five counting algorithms compared by the bursts they allow and the memory each client costs.
- [Redis vs Memcached](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/redis-vs-memcached.md): A pure cache or a data structure server: decide by whether you need more than GET and SET.
- [REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/rest-vs-grpc-vs-graphql.md): Choose an API style by who the client is, and whether you control it.
- [Senior vs staff: how the same question is graded differently](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/senior-vs-staff-expectations.md): The same question, graded differently by level, and what the interviewer listens for at each one.
- [Sharding strategies](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/sharding-strategies.md): Five ways to map a row to a machine, and the query each one makes expensive.
- [SQL vs NoSQL](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/sql-vs-nosql.md): Relational, document, key-value, or wide-column, chosen by the queries the product actually makes.
- [Strong vs eventual consistency](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/strong-vs-eventual-consistency.md): Which read is allowed to be stale, and who would notice: the question that picks a consistency model.
- [System design in one page](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/system-design-in-one-page.md): The whole framework, the key patterns, and the numbers, condensed. Bookmark this. Expand any line through the links.
- [Trade-off decision guides](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/trade-offs.md): Interviews reward reasoning about trade-offs, not memorized answers. Here are the common "X vs Y" decisions and how to choose, each with a one-line answer you can say out loud.
- [WebSockets vs SSE vs long polling](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/cheat-sheets/websockets-vs-sse-vs-long-polling.md): Choose a real-time transport by which way the messages travel, and how often.

## Patterns

The reusable building blocks. Learn these once and they apply to every design question.

- [API gateway](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/api-gateway.md): A single entry point in front of your services that handles auth, rate limiting, routing, and other cross-cutting concerns once.
- [Backpressure](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/backpressure.md): When a system cannot keep up, it must push back on its callers instead of buffering until it dies.
- [Batch vs stream processing](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/batch-vs-stream-processing.md): Two ways to compute over large data: process accumulated data on a schedule, or process each event as it arrives.
- [Bloom filters](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/bloom-filters.md): A small, fast structure that tells you an item is "definitely not present" or "possibly present", using very little memory.
- [Caching](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/caching.md): Store the results of expensive work close to where they are needed, so repeated reads are fast and cheap.
- [CAP theorem](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/cap-theorem.md): In a distributed system, when a network partition happens, you can keep either consistency or availability, not both.
- [CDN (content delivery network)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/cdn.md): A network of edge servers that cache content close to users, cutting latency and offloading your origin.
- [Checksums](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/checksums.md): A small fingerprint computed from data, checked after transfer or storage to detect corruption.
- [Circuit breaker](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/circuit-breaker.md): When a downstream dependency starts failing, stop calling it for a while and fail fast, so one sick service does not take down the whole system.
- [Consistency models](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/consistency-models.md): The contract for what a read is allowed to return when data is replicated and being written concurrently.
- [Consistent hashing](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/consistent-hashing.md): Distribute keys across nodes so that adding or removing a node moves as little data as possible.
- [Database indexing](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/database-indexing.md): A data structure that lets the database find rows by a key without scanning the whole table.
- [Distributed locking](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/distributed-locking.md): Mutual exclusion across machines: make sure at most one process in the whole system does a thing at a time.
- [Distributed transactions: 2PC vs sagas](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/distributed-transactions.md): Keep one logical operation correct when it spans services that each own their own database.
- [Event sourcing and CQRS](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/event-sourcing-cqrs.md): Store what happened as the source of truth, and build every view you need by replaying it.
- [Gossip protocol](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/gossip-protocol.md): Nodes learn the state of a large cluster by periodically exchanging what they know with a few random peers.
- [Heartbeats and failure detection](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/heartbeats.md): Nodes periodically say "I'm alive" so the system can tell a dead server from a slow one and react automatically.
- [Idempotency](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/idempotency.md): Design operations so that doing them twice has the same effect as doing them once, making retries safe.
- [Leader election (leader and follower)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/leader-election.md): Pick one node to be in charge of a task or a data partition, and pick a new one automatically when it fails.
- [Load balancing](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/load-balancing.md): Spread incoming traffic across multiple servers so no single one is overwhelmed, and so the system stays available when a server fails.
- [Logical clocks: Lamport and vector clocks](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/logical-clocks.md): Order events across machines with counters, because wall clocks on different servers cannot be trusted to agree.
- [Long polling vs WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/long-polling-websockets-sse.md): Three ways to push real-time updates from server to client, from "good enough" to fully bidirectional.
- [Message queues](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/message-queues.md): Put a buffer between producers and consumers so work can be processed asynchronously and the two sides scale independently.
- [Outbox pattern](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/outbox-pattern.md): Publish events reliably by writing them to your own database first, then letting a relay push them out.
- [Proxies](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/proxies.md): An intermediary server that sits between clients and servers, used for routing, security, caching, and hiding topology.
- [Quorum](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/quorum.md): Require a minimum number of replicas to agree before a read or write counts, so the system stays correct when some nodes are down.
- [Rate limiting](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/rate-limiting.md): Cap how many requests a client can make in a time window, to protect a service from overload and abuse.
- [Replication](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/replication.md): Keep copies of data on multiple nodes so the system stays available when one fails, and so reads can scale.
- [Sharding and partitioning](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/sharding-partitioning.md): Split a dataset across multiple machines so it can grow beyond what a single database can hold or serve.
- [Write-ahead log (WAL)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/patterns/write-ahead-log.md): Record every change to an append-only log before applying it, so a crash never loses acknowledged data.

## System design questions

Walkthroughs at the level of approach, key decisions, and trade-offs.

- [Design an ad click aggregator](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-ad-click-aggregator.md): Ingest a massive stream of ad click events and produce accurate, near real-time aggregated counts.
- [Design an AI agent orchestration system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-ai-agent-orchestration.md): A platform that runs LLM agents: multi-step loops where a model plans, calls tools, observes results, and continues until a task completes.
- [Design Airbnb](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-airbnb.md): A marketplace to search listings by location and dates, view availability, and book without double-booking.
- [Design Amazon Lambda (serverless functions)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-amazon-lambda.md): A platform that runs user functions on demand, scaling automatically, without users managing servers.
- [Design Amazon S3 (object storage)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-amazon-s3.md): A durable, scalable object store: put, get, and delete large blobs by key, with very high durability.
- [Design Amazon shopping cart](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-amazon-shopping-cart.md): A cart that holds items per user, persists across devices and sessions, and feeds into checkout.
- [Design an API gateway](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-api-gateway.md): A single entry point in front of many backend services that handles routing, auth, and cross-cutting concerns.
- [Design ChatGPT (LLM serving)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-chatgpt.md): A service that serves a large language model to many users, streaming responses with low latency.
- [Design an AI code assistant (Copilot)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-code-assistant.md): Serve code completions inside the editor at keystroke speed, grounded in the user's own repository.
- [Design a code deployment system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-code-deployment-system.md): Build, distribute, and roll out application binaries to a large fleet of servers safely.
- [Design a code judging system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-code-judging-system.md): Accept code submissions, run them against test cases in a sandbox, and return a verdict, safely and at scale.
- [Design a collaborative whiteboard (Miro)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-collaborative-whiteboard.md): A shared canvas where many users draw and edit shapes together in real time.
- [Design Discord](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-discord.md): A community chat platform with servers, channels, real-time messaging, presence, and voice.
- [Design a distributed cache (like Redis)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-distributed-cache.md): An in-memory key-value cache spread across many nodes, for fast reads and reduced load on the data store.
- [Design a distributed job scheduler (like Cron)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-distributed-job-scheduler.md): Run jobs at scheduled times or intervals across a fleet, reliably and exactly as intended.
- [Design a distributed message queue](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-distributed-message-queue.md): Build the queue itself: durable, ordered, high-throughput delivery of messages from producers to consumers.
- [Design Dropbox](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-dropbox.md): A cloud storage service that stores files and syncs them across a user's devices, with sharing.
- [Design a flash sale system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-flash-sale-system.md): Sell a limited quantity of items to a massive burst of concurrent buyers, without overselling.
- [Design a food delivery app (DoorDash)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-food-delivery.md): A three-sided marketplace: customers order, restaurants cook, couriers deliver, and the system keeps all three in sync.
- [Design a real-time gaming leaderboard](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-gaming-leaderboard.md): Rank tens of millions of players by score, update the ranking after every match, and read the top of the board cheaply.
- [Design Gmail](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-gmail.md): An email service to send, receive, store, search, and organize mail at large scale.
- [Design Google Ads](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-google-ads.md): An ad platform that selects and serves ads, tracks clicks, and bills advertisers accurately.
- [Design Google Calendar](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-google-calendar.md): A calendar service with events, recurring events, invitations, reminders, and availability.
- [Design Google Docs](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-google-docs.md): A collaborative document editor where many people edit the same document at once and see changes live.
- [Design Google Maps](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-google-maps.md): Serve the map, compute routes, and estimate arrival times for a billion users.
- [Design Google News](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-google-news.md): Aggregate articles from many sources, group them by story, rank them, and personalize a news feed.
- [Design Google Search](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-google-search.md): Crawl the web, build an index, and return ranked results for a query within milliseconds.
- [Design a GPU cluster scheduler](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-gpu-cluster-scheduler.md): The system that decides which ML jobs run on which GPUs: thousands of accelerators, training jobs that need hundreds of them at once, and inference that cannot wait.
- [Design a hotel reservation system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-hotel-reservation.md): Search rooms by city and dates, then book without double-booking, across a date range, at chain scale.
- [Design Instagram](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-instagram.md): A photo-sharing service where users post images, follow others, and see a feed of posts from people they follow.
- [Design LinkedIn connections](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-linkedin-connections.md): A professional social graph with connection requests, degrees of connection, and the people graph.
- [Design a live comment streaming service (Twitch chat)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-live-comment-streaming.md): Broadcast a high-volume stream of live comments to many concurrent viewers in real time.
- [Design an LLM gateway](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-llm-gateway.md): One API in front of every model provider: routing, quotas, caching, failover, and a cost meter for every team.
- [Design an LLM inference platform](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-llm-inference-platform.md): The serving layer behind a ChatGPT-style product: run large models on GPU fleets, stream tokens to millions of users, and keep cost per request sane.
- [Design a metrics and monitoring system (like Datadog or Prometheus)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-metrics-monitoring.md): Collect, store, and query time-series metrics from many services, with dashboards and alerts.
- [Design a model evaluation pipeline](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-model-evaluation-pipeline.md): A system that continuously measures model quality: run benchmark suites against model versions, compare candidates against production, and gate releases on the results.
- [Design Netflix](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-netflix.md): A video streaming service that ingests, encodes, and streams video to a global audience, with browse and recommendations.
- [Design a notification system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-notification-system.md): A service that sends notifications to users across multiple channels (push, email, SMS, in-app) reliably and at scale.
- [Design a payment system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-payment-system.md): Process payments reliably, without double-charging, with an accurate record of every transaction.
- [Design "People You May Know" (Facebook)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-people-you-may-know.md): Suggest people a user might know, primarily from mutual connections in the social graph.
- [Design a proximity service (Yelp)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-proximity-service.md): Given a location, return nearby businesses, filtered and ranked, at read-heavy scale.
- [Design a RAG pipeline](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-rag-pipeline.md): A retrieval-augmented generation system: answer user questions over a private document corpus by retrieving relevant passages and feeding them to an LLM.
- [Design a rate limiter](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-rate-limiter.md): A service that limits how many requests a client can make in a time window, shared across a fleet of servers.
- [Design a recommendation system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-recommendation-system.md): Suggest relevant items (videos, products, posts) to each user, personalized and at scale.
- [Design Reddit](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-reddit.md): A community platform with subreddits, posts, nested comments, voting, and ranked feeds.
- [Design a reminder and alert system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-reminder-alert-system.md): Fire reminders at their scheduled time, at scale, reliably, even for millions of pending reminders.
- [Design semantic search (vector search)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-semantic-search.md): A search service that matches by meaning rather than keywords: embed items and queries as vectors, then find nearest neighbors at scale.
- [Design a stock exchange](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-stock-exchange.md): A trading system that matches buy and sell orders fairly, with very low latency and strict correctness.
- [Design Ticketmaster](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-ticketmaster.md): Sell seats to live events without ever selling the same seat twice, and survive the moment tickets go on sale.
- [Design TinyURL](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-tinyurl.md): A URL shortening service that turns a long URL into a short, unique alias and redirects users from the alias to the original.
- [Design Twitter](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-twitter.md): A microblogging service where users post short messages (tweets) and see a timeline of tweets from accounts they follow.
- [Design typeahead / autocomplete](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-typeahead-autocomplete.md): Suggest completions as a user types, ranked by popularity, with very low latency.
- [Design Uber](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-uber.md): A ride-hailing service that matches riders with nearby drivers in real time and tracks the trip.
- [Design a unique ID generator](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-unique-id-generator.md): Generate globally unique IDs at high throughput, ideally roughly sortable by time, with no collisions.
- [Design a web crawler](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-web-crawler.md): A system that systematically browses the web, fetching pages and following links, for example to build a search index.
- [Design WhatsApp](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-whatsapp.md): A real-time messaging service for one-to-one and group chats, with delivery status and presence.
- [Design a likes counter (YouTube)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-youtube-likes-counter.md): Count likes for billions of items at very high write rates, with near real-time, approximately accurate reads.
- [Design YouTube](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-youtube.md): A video platform to upload, process, store, and stream videos to a global audience, with search and recommendations.
- [Design Zoom](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/design-zoom.md): Multi-party video calls that feel instant, worldwide, even on bad networks.
- [Practice question bank](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/questions/practice-bank.md): Prompts to test yourself against, with no solutions here on purpose.

## Distributed systems deep dives

How landmark systems actually work, the "how does X work" questions common in senior interviews.

- [Aurora: rethinking the database for the cloud](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/aurora-cloud-native-database.md): Amazon's cloud-native relational database, built on one idea: the log is the database, so replicate the log, not the pages.
- [BigTable: a wide-column store](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/bigtable-wide-column-store.md): A table can hold petabytes of rows, and every read into it starts from one place: the row key.
- [Borg and Kubernetes: cluster management](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/borg-kubernetes.md): Run every job in a datacenter on a shared pool of machines, and keep them running when machines die.
- [Cassandra: a wide-column NoSQL database](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/cassandra-wide-column-db.md): A database with no leader at all: every node is equal, so any node can accept your write and any node can answer your read.
- [Chubby: a distributed locking service](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/chubby-distributed-locking.md): Five machines run Paxos so that thousands of other machines can agree on one leader, one config value, and one address.
- [Dynamo: a distributed key-value store](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/dynamo-key-value-store.md): A store that accepts your write even when the machines that own the key are down, then hands you two versions later.
- [DynamoDB: the managed database that never falls over](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/dynamodb-managed-nosql.md): A table that answers in a few milliseconds whether it holds ten items or ten billion, because the service removed almost every knob.
- [Elasticsearch and Lucene: search internals](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/elasticsearch-lucene.md): How full-text search actually works, from the inverted index up to a distributed search cluster.
- [Flink: stateful stream processing](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/flink-stream-processing.md): Compute continuously over unbounded streams, keep large state, and still get correct results after a crash.
- [GFS: the Google File System](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/gfs-distributed-file-system.md): Files of many gigabytes, written by appending and read from start to end, stored on cheap machines that are expected to break.
- [HDFS: the Hadoop Distributed File System](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/hdfs-file-storage.md): One machine remembers where every block lives, a thousand machines hold the bytes, and nothing already written can be changed.
- [HNSW and vector databases](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/hnsw-vector-search.md): Find the nearest vectors among billions, fast, by giving up the guarantee that they are exactly the nearest.
- [Kafka: a distributed messaging system](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/kafka-distributed-messaging.md): Every event is written to disk and kept after it is read, which is why Kafka is fast and why you can replay last week.
- [MapReduce: batch processing at scale](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/mapreduce-batch-processing.md): A job runs on a thousand machines for six hours, some of them die while it runs, and nobody has to wake up.
- [Memcached at Facebook: caching at planet scale](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/memcached-at-facebook.md): A write here does not update the cache. It deletes the entry, and a short token decides which single client is allowed to refill it.
- [Raft: understandable consensus](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/raft-consensus.md): Consensus cut into three parts you can hold in your head: elect one leader, copy its log, and never elect a leader that is missing a committed entry.
- [Redis internals](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/redis-internals.md): How a single-threaded in-memory server serves a million operations a second, and what it does to survive a restart.
- [Spanner: globally consistent SQL](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/spanner-global-sql.md): A database that reads physical clocks, admits how wrong they might be, and waits that error out before it says "committed".
- [ZooKeeper: coordination as a service](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/deep-dives/zookeeper-coordination.md): A tiny replicated file tree, kept in one strict order by a majority vote, that other systems use to decide who is in charge.

## Study roadmaps

Time-boxed study plans, plus one diagnostic-led plan for experienced engineers.

- [1-week crash plan](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/roadmaps/1-week-plan.md): Triage for an interview a few days away, at two to three hours a day: the essentials and practice, nothing else.
- [2-week system design sprint](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/roadmaps/2-week-plan.md): A focused sprint at one to two hours a day, for an interview a couple of weeks out.
- [6-week study plan](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/roadmaps/6-week-plan.md): Build real depth from a baseline at about an hour a day, covering all 30 patterns and all 19 deep dives.
- [Senior and staff refresher](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-system-design/blob/main/roadmaps/senior-staff-refresher.md): For experienced engineers who have not interviewed in years: a cold diagnostic first, then only the gaps it finds.
